channel.title: Fixture Science Wire
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news.

item.title: Space telescope spots water vapour on a distant planet
item.description: Astronomers using a space telescope have detected water vapour in the atmosphere of a planet 120 light years away. The planet is about twice the size of Earth.

item.title: Scientists map the ocean floor near Antarctica in new detail
item.description: A research ship has mapped 50,000 square kilometres of sea floor near Antarctica. The maps reveal underwater canyons and an extinct volcano.

item.title: Study finds city trees cut summer temperatures by 2 degrees
item.description: A study of 90 European cities found that streets with many trees were about 2 degrees cooler in summer. Researchers say parks also reduced heat-related illness.

item.title: Rover finds layered rocks in an ancient lake bed on Mars
item.description: A Mars rover has photographed layered rocks in what scientists believe was an ancient lake bed. The layers could hold clues about past water on the planet.

item.title: New species of glowing mushroom found in Brazilian forest
item.description: Biologists have described a new species of glowing mushroom found in the Atlantic forest of Brazil. It emits a soft green light at night.

item.title: Astronauts grow tomatoes on the space station
item.description: Astronauts on the International Space Station have harvested tomatoes grown in a small greenhouse. Scientists want to learn how to feed crews on long missions.

item.title: Solar eclipse to be visible across northern Spain next August
item.description: A total solar eclipse will be visible across northern Spain next August. Astronomers say the shadow will cross Bilbao and Valencia.

item.title: Researchers teach a robot hand to tie shoelaces
item.description: Engineers have trained a robot hand to tie shoelaces using two fingers and a thumb. The robot learned the task in simulation before trying it for real.

item.title: Bees use the sun as a compass even on cloudy days, study says
item.description: A new study shows honeybees can find the sun's position through clouds using polarised light. The finding explains how they navigate in poor weather.

item.title: Comet will pass close enough to see with binoculars this week
item.description: A comet discovered last year will pass close to Earth this week and should be visible with binoculars just after sunset.

item.title: Coral reef shows signs of recovery off Australia
item.description: Scientists surveying a section of reef off Queensland, Australia, say coral cover has increased for the third year in a row.
